title: Finite chart formulas for double-plane equations divisible by an exceptional parameter
statement:
Let $(S,\mathfrak n,k)$ be a commutative Noetherian local domain of dimension $2$ [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring]. Suppose $u,v,w$ minimally generate $\mathfrak n$ and their initial forms identify $\operatorname{gr}_{\mathfrak n}S$ with $k[U,V,W]/(W^2)$ [def-weil-pbc-associated-graded-ring], [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring]. Form ordinary blowups at the closed point [def-nagata-global-blowup], [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. In each assertion below, $S'$ denotes the local ring of the blowup at the specified $k$-rational point of the exceptional line (so its residue field is $k$), and it is ASSUMED, as a hypothesis of that assertion, that the three chart generators named there generate its maximal ideal $\mathfrak n'$ and identify its associated graded ring with $k[T_1,T_2,T_3]/(q')$ for a nonzero quadratic polynomial $q'$ which is a scalar times a square. (Without this hypothesis the successor may be regular or have a non-square tangent quadratic.) There is no assumption about any infinite sequence.
(1) Write $w^2=J$ with $J\in\mathfrak n^3$ and expand $J$ as a sum of degree-three monomials in $u,v,w$ with coefficients in $S$. If the successor is in the $u$-chart, put $t=v/u-\widetilde\lambda$ and $z=w/u$, where $\lambda\in k$ is its coordinate on the exceptional line and $\widetilde\lambda\in S$ is any lift. There is a lift $\delta\in S'$ of an element of $k$ such that $u,t,\omega=z+\delta u$ minimally generate its maximal ideal $\mathfrak n'$, $q'=W_{\omega}^2$ up to a nonzero scalar, and $\omega^2=uF'$ for some $F'\in(\mathfrak n')^2$.
For (2) and (3), assume more specifically that $w^2=uF$ with $F\in\mathfrak n^2$. Express its degree-two class in $\mathfrak n^2/\mathfrak n^3$ as a quadratic in $U,V,W$ modulo $W^2$, and put $H(U,V)=U(aV^2+bUV+cU^2)$, where $a,b,c\in k$ are the coefficients of $V^2,UV,U^2$ respectively; this is the binary cubic obtained by setting $W=0$ in the relation for $w^2$.
(2) Suppose $a\ne0$ and $[1:\lambda]$ is a multiple zero of $H$. At this successor in the $u$-chart one can choose $\omega=z+\delta u$ as in (1), with $\omega^2=uF'$ and $F'\in(\mathfrak n')^2$, so that its binary cubic is $H'(U,T)=U(aT^2+b'UT+c'U^2)$ for some $b',c'\in k$. The element $u$ generates the exceptional-divisor ideal in $S'$.
(3) Suppose $a=0$, and take the successor $[0:1]$ in the $v$-chart, with generators $v,r=u/v,z=w/v$. Then $q'=Z^2$ up to a nonzero scalar, and there is $L\in\mathfrak n'$ with the exact identity $z^2=vrL$. Its binary cubic is $H'(V,R)=VR(bR+eV)$ for some $e\in k$. In particular, if $b\ne0$ the coefficient of $VR^2$ is $b$; if $b=0$ and $H'\ne0$, then $e\ne0$ and the same cubic is $R(eV^2)$, while $z^2=r(vL)$ and $vL\in(\mathfrak n')^2$. These identities hold in every residue characteristic, including characteristic $2$.
